nodes.label: Session Handoff Protocol
nodes.rationale: Cross-session coordination: cloud session writes tasks, Cowork/desktop session executes them; tracker stays single source of truth and Umair approves all submits/sends.

nodes.label: Human-Approval Guardrails
nodes.rationale: Agent prepares, human fires: user always clicks Submit and approves outreach sends; no fabrication, no LinkedIn automation (ToS), no guessed email addresses.

nodes.label: Master Resume (Source of Truth)
nodes.rationale: Deliberately longer than any sendable resume; /tailor-resume cuts it down per job and never invents anything not in this file.

nodes.label: Job Scoring Rubric
nodes.rationale: Weighted 0-10 score (title 3, location 2, salary 2, industry 1, seniority 1, no dealbreakers 1); only 7+ enter the tracker, 5-6 are borderline, below 5 dropped silently.

nodes.label: Candidate Profile
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth read by every skill; forms are filled with exactly what is written here to keep answers consistent and prevent fabrication.

nodes.label: Search Playbook
nodes.rationale: Read before each /find-jobs round, round log appended after — every sourcing round is meant to be sharper than the last.

nodes.label: ATS-Domain-Scoped Search
nodes.rationale: Constraining search to ATS domains (greenhouse/lever/ashby etc.) returns direct applyable posting URLs instead of near-useless aggregator landing pages; proven in Round 3 and now the default first move.

nodes.label: PrepChef Overview
nodes.rationale: Docs 01-04 drafted against a one-paragraph vision, then reconciled with the founder's full vision: meal-prep-first, macro targets without tracking, curated locale packs, constrained assistant.

nodes.label: Product Critique
nodes.rationale: Meal planning is a graveyard category: personalized-plan products demo well and churn in 2-6 weeks; building the same thing with an LLM inherits the churn curve with higher COGS.

nodes.label: Stress-Removal Wedge
nodes.rationale: Four value props is zero value props; 'what's for dinner' stress is the only daily, emotional pain — savings and waste become proof metrics, 'healthier' becomes a default bias, not a feature.

nodes.label: Plan Repair System
nodes.rationale: The retention killer is the plan-vs-reality gap; the product is a plan repair system, not a plan generator. Deviation is the main case, and replanning under messy natural-language constraints is where an LLM beats rule engines.

nodes.label: Cooked/Skipped Feedback Loop
nodes.rationale: One prompt per planned meal — Cooked 👍 / Cooked 👎 / Skipped, three buttons no forms — the cheapest way to feed the preference graph moat.

nodes.label: Household Preference Graph
nodes.rationale: The defensible moat: what this household cooked, skipped, swapped, rated over months. Week 12's plan should beat week 1's, and the data doesn't port to a competitor. The LLM is interface and constraint-solver, not the moat.

nodes.label: Curated Recipe Corpus
nodes.rationale: Scraping is legally grey; pure LLM recipes are untested and one inedible meal destroys trust. ~300-500 curated recipes with structured ingredients; the AI selects, sequences, scales, adapts — never invents recipes in v1.

nodes.label: Tracker Trap
nodes.rationale: Macro meters and food logging pull the product toward MyFitnessPal, whose engagement demands are brutal. PrepChef's promise is the opposite: follow the plan and the numbers take care of themselves — no logging, no calorie-remaining meter.

nodes.label: Locale Packs
nodes.rationale: Real localization is curated data work per locale (availability, naming, cost bands, halal defaults) — an 'any country' dropdown guarantees fake output. v1 ships two curated packs: Pakistan and US.

nodes.label: Constrained AI Assistant
nodes.rationale: Open-ended chat is an unbounded cost/failure surface that competes with ChatGPT and loses. Every vision example is a plan operation with parameters: intent parsing → structured ops → the same validated pipeline, with a visible capability menu.

nodes.label: Cost Bands
nodes.rationale: Dollar-precise cost estimates without price data are fabrications wearing a UI; locale-relative bands ($/$$/$$$) are deliverable and useful. Real prices are a v2 partnership problem.

nodes.label: Household-Centric Data Model
nodes.rationale: Dinner is a household decision — one picky kid vetoes a plan for four. Household-centric schema is cheap now and brutally expensive to retrofit.

nodes.label: MVP Core Loop
nodes.rationale: Onboard → targets → generated week (batch sessions) → review/adjust → grocery list → guided prep → daily feedback → mid-week repair → recap → better next week.

nodes.label: Four-Week Retention Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: The one hypothesis that matters: will a household let PrepChef plan the week and come back four weeks in a row? Bar: week-4 planning retention ≥ 35%, ≥ 60% plan execution, 👍 rate improving.

nodes.label: Meal-Prep-First Cooking Model
nodes.rationale: 1-2 batch cook sessions cover the week's lunches and dinners; breakfast is a template rotation and snacks a suggestion list — full daily macro totals without 28 generated meals per week.

nodes.label: Cut-Line Discipline
nodes.rationale: If forced to cut: recap → billing → share link → print → second locale pack. Never cut prep schedule, repair, feedback buttons, grocery consolidation, macro-fitted generation — that set is the product.

nodes.label: Hard Filters (Diet & Allergen)
nodes.rationale: FR-3: allergies and dietary preference are absolute filters at every surface, enforced by deterministic code and never left to the LLM; zero violations is a deploy-blocking correctness requirement.

nodes.label: Nutrition Targets Engine (Mifflin-St Jeor)
nodes.rationale: FR-6/7/8: BMR → TDEE → calorie and macro targets as pure unit-tested functions, never the LLM; adherence view instead of logging; clinically safe editing bounds and disclaimer.

nodes.label: Weekly Plan Generation
nodes.rationale: FR-9..14: batch recipes selected from the curated corpus under a priority-ordered constraint stack (hard filters, locale availability, ±10% macro fit, time/skill/equipment, budget, ingredient overlap, taste, variety, season).

nodes.label: AI Assistant Command Layer
nodes.rationale: FR-18/19/20: free text parses to typed operations; every result is a proposed diff requiring confirmation; unparseable requests get an honest capability menu, never a hallucinated action.

nodes.label: Consolidated Grocery List
nodes.rationale: FR-21..24: canonical-ingredient aggregation, unit normalization, household scaling, pantry-staples subtraction; offline check-off; checked items never silently vanish when de-planned.

nodes.label: Prep Schedule
nodes.rationale: FR-25/26: ordered task plan per prep session with time estimates and parallelization hints — a derived view of the plan, not a separately generated artifact, so it stays consistent under swaps and repairs.

nodes.label: Weekly Recap
nodes.rationale: FR-33: meals eaten, prep completed, protein adherence, ingredient utilization, labeled savings estimate — the weekly proof-of-value and word-of-mouth moment, guilt-free framing.

nodes.label: Information Architecture
nodes.rationale: One center of gravity — the week's plan — with Today as the daily front door; no recipe-browser identity, recipes reached only through the plan.

nodes.label: Diff Confirmation Pattern
nodes.rationale: All AI mutations render as before/after diffs with one Confirm — applies uniformly to assistant commands, repairs, and regenerations.

nodes.label: Mid-Week Repair Flow
nodes.rationale: One-tap 'didn't happen' or free-text repair → reflow prioritizing bought perishables → before/after diff → Confirm; zero guilt copy anywhere in the flow.

nodes.label: Database Design (Postgres/Supabase)
nodes.rationale: Household is the tenant (RLS boundary) even while v1 UX is single-user; recipes/ingredients are world-readable content, plans/feedback are tenant data; all nutrition numbers computed by code, the LLM never writes numbers.

nodes.label: preference_signals (table)
nodes.rationale: Append-only signal log ('the moat') — onboarding likes, feedback verdicts, swaps, exclusions with weights, aggregated with time decay into the taste profile at generation time.

nodes.label: Technical Architecture
nodes.rationale: Next.js + Supabase endorsed for a 1-2 person team; one deployable, no microservices/queues/Redis in v1. The interesting architecture is the AI planning pipeline and the discipline around what the LLM may and may not do.

nodes.label: AI Planning Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Doctrine: the LLM chooses; code computes and enforces. FILTER (SQL) → SCORE (TS) → SELECT (LLM, structured output over a compact scored table) → VALIDATE (TS) → DERIVE → PERSIST+LOG. Correctness never depends on model behavior; small structured calls keep cost low; each step is swappable.

nodes.label: Eval & Safety Harness (Golden Households)
nodes.rationale: ~30 synthetic households crossing locales, diets, allergies, budgets, equipment; CI asserts zero hard-filter violations, macro fit, overlap floor, latency. Prompt/model/corpus changes must pass the harness.

nodes.label: Greedy Fallback Assembler
nodes.rationale: Pure-code plan assembly always available — slightly less clever, never wrong — so the product degrades instead of going down during an LLM API outage or repeated validation failure.

nodes.label: Inference Cost Model
nodes.rationale: Target ≤ $0.30/active user/month: Sonnet for generation (~$0.027), Haiku for ops, prompt-cached preamble, per-household daily op budget enforced in code — COGS must not scale with engagement.

nodes.label: Implementation Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Six milestones (M0-M6), each ending runnable with a kill/keep decision; content pipeline and eval harness come early because they gate everything; daily-loop features precede polish because they are the retention hypothesis; billing last.

nodes.label: Content Pipeline
nodes.rationale: The long pole: ingredient dictionary, validation/ingest scripts, nutrition computation, recipe_locales materialization, human verification flags; 50-recipe proof in M1, corpus to ~350 as a parallel workstream through M4.
